children: Korn Ferry logged higher net income and revenue in its fiscal first quarter, boosted in part by continued growth across its executive search business.
The consulting firm reported net income of $69 million, or $1.32 a share, for its three months ended July 31, up from $66.6 million, or $1.26 a share, the year prior.
Stripping out one-time items, earnings were $1.43 a share. Analysts polled by FactSet expected adjusted earnings of $1.36 a share.
Total revenue came in at $764.6 million, up from $715.5 million a year ago.

Fee revenue was up 6.8% to $756.5 million, ahead of Wall Street models for $737.7 million. Fee revenue rose across all regions, led by double-digit growth in search and workforce solutions, the company said.

Chief Executive Gary Burnison said the recent quarter marked Korn Ferry's sixth consecutive quarter of top-line growth, demonstrating the momentum and durability of its business. The company has benefited from its acquisition of AMS, he added, which has complemented and meaningfully expanded its operations.

Looking ahead, Korn Ferry guided for adjusted earnings of $1.30 to $1.40 on fee revenue of $860 million to $878 million in the current quarter. That compares with analyst views for adjusted earnings of $1.46 a share on fee revenue of $742.5 million.
